rationale.conceptual: The central bursting criterion (Equation 37) is a long, custom expression with multiple composite trigonometric terms and auxiliary functions (A(α), B(α), f(α)). Transcribing it correctly from a scanned 1970 paper and handling domain pitfalls (log arguments, singularities) requires careful implementation, but the method itself is established upper-bound mechanics. It sits at the level of a non-trivial, multi-part documented algorithm.
rationale.execution: The task is a single-step script: implement the inequality, run a parameter sweep, perform 1D root-finding, and output one CSV. No multi-stage orchestration, external tooling, or complex I/O is needed; standard Python with numpy/scipy suffices.
